acceptance_criteria.criterion: A new numbered section exists in edge-cases.md (after §21.70) documenting the cross-WP dispatch edge case
The section describes the stall scenario, the resolution via findNextReadyDispatch(), the self-routing behavior, and the invariant that cross-WP dispatch is best-effort for IDE runners
The section references the relevant handoff spec section (§13.1 or the new findNextReadyDispatch subsection)

summary: Added §21.71 Cross-WP Dispatch from Non-PM Agents to edge-cases.md immediately after §21.70. The new section documents: (1) the IDE stall scenario where a non-PM agent returns WAIT after completing WP-001's final stage with WP-002 sitting READY, (2) the resolution via findNextReadyDispatch() inserted as the penultimate step in each of the five affected handoff functions, (3) the self-routing behavior and design rationale (IDE audit trail / orchestrator alignment), and (4) the invariant that cross-WP dispatch is best-effort for IDE runners only. The section references §13.5 (findNextReadyDispatch algorithm) and §13.1 (per-agent handoff functions) per acceptance criteria.

comments.note: Section §21.71 is structured with three named subsections (Stall scenario, Resolution, Self-routing, Invariant) matching the depth and style of §21.70 and other recent additions. The self-routing example uses a documentation-only WP to make the same-agent dispatch concrete. No reviewer-forwarded items were present in the code-review pipeline (documentation-only pipeline chain for this WP).
